LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading fluency, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read a text fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in collaboration with others, read sentences and express different emotions as written on flash cards. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,

2. discuss the different intonation patterns found in the sentences and report to the class. Learners with speech

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in collaboration with others, read sentences and express different emotions as written on flash cards. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,
2. discuss the different intonation patterns found in the sentences and report to the class. Learners with speech

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy as learner ensures access to appropriate resources as they listen to audiobooks and work with others to

identify features of expressive reading such as pitch, pace and volume.

Values:
Integrity is enhanced as the learner practices honesty as they work in pairs to identify examples of expressive reading.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Life Skills Education-peer pressure resistance: The learners’ ability to cope with peer pressure is enhanced as they record

the readings and share them with others online.
